findings.title: The CLI reads the wallet contract with offset paging and no fixed order, so a page can skip or repeat a UTxO
findings.scenario:
The CLI's balance, transfer, sweep, remove, fund and util mint all read every Seedelf UTxO of every user with `credential_utxos(wallet_contract_hash)`. That is thousands of rows, so several 1,000-row pages, each fetched with `?offset=N`, no `order=` and no `limit=`. Suppose a block lands between two page requests (another user's Seedelf spend, or a stranger taking back junk UTxOs parked at the contract, since a non-Register datum is spendable by anyone). A row removed below the offset moves every later row up by one, so the row at the page boundary is never read. With no `order=`, the database may also return rows in a different order on each request, which can both drop and repeat rows. Possible outcomes for that read:
- an owned UTxO is missing, so balance shows less, or fund/transfer misses the recipient's seedelf and stops;
- an owned UTxO is counted twice, so balance overstates by its value, and a spend that picks it twice builds a transaction the node refuses.

Nothing is lost, but the figure is wrong for that run.
findings.evidence:
seedelf-koios/src/koios.rs:243-269: `let mut offset: i32 = 0; loop { ... .post(url.clone()) ... .query(&[("offset", offset.to_string())]) .json(&payload) ... let mut utxos: Vec<UtxoResponse> = response.json().await?; if utxos.is_empty() { break; } all_utxos.append(&mut utxos); offset += 1000; }`. It sends no order and no limit, does not dedupe, and assumes the server's page is exactly 1,000 rows. address_transactions (koios.rs:831-884) does the same with `offset` and `limit=65` and no order.

Callers: seedelf-core/src/utxos.rs:13-22 `get_credential_utxos` feeds `collect_all_wallet_utxos` and `collect_wallet_utxos` (utxos.rs:32-130), which push every owned row with no outpoint dedupe.

The extension's copy was fixed for exactly this. koios.ts:1326-1342 `paged()` asks for `order=tx_hash.asc,tx_index.asc&limit=1000` with a keyset `or=(tx_hash.gt.<h>,and(tx_hash.eq.<h>,tx_index.gt.<i>))`, dedupes by `${tx_hash}#${tx_index}`, and stops on a short page. launch-review.md:256 #31: 'Offset paging over a changing UTxO set can skip or duplicate a row. | koios.ts:473 | Keyset paging, and dedupe by outpoint.' That fix was TS only.

Not run, because no network calls are allowed. Two ways to confirm: check Koios's credential_utxos SQL for an ORDER BY, or write a seedelf-koios test against a local mock (`override_endpoints`) that drops a row between page 1 and page 2.
findings.known_check: Searched docs/backlog.md and docs/archive/plans/*.md for offset, paging, paged, keyset, credential_utxos, seedelf-koios and koios.rs. launch-review #31 fixed this class in koios.ts only (that pass was wallet-only). No review, backlog line or the backlog's CLI section records the Rust copy as open or declined.

findings.title: CLI submit: a timeout or 5xx after Koios forwarded the transaction reads as failed or rejected, so running the command again can pay twice
findings.scenario: `seedelf-cli transfer` (and every command through `spend::prove_and_submit`, and `external sweep`) sends the signed CBOR with `submit_tx`. Koios forwards it to the node, but its answer never arrives: the client's 30 s timeout fires, or the gateway returns a 502 or 504. The CLI prints `Failed to submit transaction` or `Koios rejected the transaction: ... 504 Gateway Timeout`. It prints no transaction hash, because the hash is printed only after success. The transaction lands anyway. The user runs `transfer` again once that block is in. The spent inputs are gone, so the CLI picks other UTxOs and pays the recipient a second time. A re-run before it lands reuses the same inputs and the node refuses it, so the risk starts once the first transaction is on chain.
findings.evidence:
koios.rs:553-561: `HTTP_CLIENT.post(url).header("Content-Type", "application/cbor").body(data).send().await.context("Failed to submit transaction")?.error_for_status().context("Koios rejected the transaction")?;`. A client timeout (koios.rs:17-19, 30 s) and any 5xx land in these two errors, and both read as 'not sent'.

seedelf-cli/src/commands/spend.rs:91-93 prints the hash only after `fee::parse_submit_response` (fee.rs:21-28) succeeds; external/sweep.rs:61 does the same. So the user has nothing to look up.

The extension fixed the same class: launch-review.md:229 #10 (Medium), 'A submit Koios didn't answer is treated as not sent, and the retry the wallet asks for pays twice', fixed with a maybe-sent state.
findings.known_check: Searched docs/archive/plans/*.md and docs/backlog.md for 'maybe sent', 'pays twice', submit_tx and submittx. launch-review #10 fixed this class in the extension (script-spend.ts, move-in.ts, lovejoin.ts). The CLI's submit_tx appears in no review, backlog line or the backlog's CLI section. Overlaps R4, which owns spend.rs.

findings.title: schnorr::prove (exported as verifyProof, never called) panics on a z over 32 bytes, so it doesn't decide as the deployed validator does
findings.scenario: A call `verifyProof(register, z, g_r, vkh)` with a 33-byte z whose first byte is 00 and whose value is below q: a z the deployed validator accepts. `32 - z_bytes.len()` underflows. seedelf-crypto has overflow checks on in [profile.wasm-release], and a wrapped index panics anyway, so the WebAssembly traps instead of answering. No code in extension/src calls verifyProof, so nobody reaches this today.
findings.evidence:
schnorr.rs:196-198: `let z_bytes: Vec<u8> = hex::decode(z_b)...; let mut z_array: [u8; 32] = [0u8; 32]; z_array[(32 - z_bytes.len())..].copy_from_slice(&z_bytes);`.

The deployed verifier (5b82530 lib/schnorr.ak:102) uses `scalar.from_bytearray_big_endian(z_b)`. In stdlib v2.2.0 that is `new(bytearray_to_integer(True, bytes))` with `n >= 0 && n < field_prime`, so any length is taken.

The overflow checks are set at seedelf-platform/Cargo.toml:62-63. The export is wasm/src/lib.rs:6786 ('mirroring the wallet validator'), which goes through api::verify_proof at lib.rs:5206 ('the same way the wallet validator does'). `grep -rn verifyProof extension/src` finds no caller.

Also, schnorr.rs:183 and :193 say 'Failed to decompress generator' for u and g_r, as do register.rs:136 and :218 for the public value.
findings.fix: Either decode z as the validator does (strip leading zero bytes, and treat more than 32 significant bytes or a value of q or more as not a proof, Ok(false)), or drop the unused export and keep `prove` test-only. Correct the four error messages.
findings.known_check: Searched docs/archive/plans and docs/backlog.md for verifyProof, verify_proof and 'prove('. Nothing found.

findings.title: hashing::sha3_256's doc says bad hex hashes an empty array and never fails; it returns an error
findings.scenario: A caller relies on the doc and passes non-hex expecting the hash of the empty input. They get Err('Invalid Input') instead. No caller outside tests uses sha3_256, so this is wording on dead code.
findings.evidence: hashing.rs:75: 'If the input is not a valid hex string, it falls back to hashing an empty byte array.' hashing.rs:88-89: 'This function will not panic, but if `data` is not a valid hex string, it will hash an empty byte array.' The code at hashing.rs:94 is `hex::decode(data).context("Invalid Input")?`, which errors. A grep finds no use of sha3_256 outside seedelf-crypto/tests.
findings.fix: Say 'errors on invalid hex', as blake2b_224 and blake2b_256 above it do, or remove the unused function.
findings.known_check: Searched docs/archive/plans and docs/backlog.md for sha3 and hashing.rs. Nothing found.

guards.stops: A proof whose Fiat-Shamir input isn't a 28-byte one-time key hash. Without that binding, a proof could be replayed after a rollback.

Nonce reuse across two statements, which would reveal the Seedelf key and with it every private UTxO and Lovejoin box. The nonce is HMAC-SHA-512 keyed by sk over the statement plus 32 fresh random bytes.
guards.test: seedelf-crypto/tests/schnorr_test.rs create_proof_draws_a_new_nonce_each_time. It checks freshness only; no test pins the hedge with a repeated random source.

guards.stops: Proving for a register outside the prime-order subgroup (defense in depth).
Re-randomizing an off-curve or torsion register, which would write a permanently locked UTxO. `from_compressed` is the real check; the explicit check at lines 141-147 can never fail.
guards.test: none found in seedelf-crypto. Payees are covered through core's is_payable tests.

guards.stops: A different d on the two points, which makes a dead UTxO.
Treating a stranger's anyone-can-spend register with an identity point as the user's own, which would make a wrong balance figure and spends that race others.
guards.test: seedelf-crypto/tests/register_test.rs identity_register_is_owned_by_no_key, identity_public_value_is_owned_by_no_key, identity_generator_is_owned_by_no_key; seedelf-core/tests/utxos_test.rs wallet_scans_skip_an_identity_register

guards.stops: A zero mix witness. Its output box would be the identity pair, which anyone can withdraw.
guards.test: none found (core's nonzero_scalar also prevents it)

guards.stops: A zero secret in an owner Schnorr proof (also checked in derive_nonce at line 131).
A sigma-OR with N outside [2, 255], whose 1-byte N prefix would not match the validator's.
guards.test: none found. lovejoins_negatives_are_refused covers verification failures, not N.

guards.stops: Overpaying every fee, minimum and deposit on a wrong Koios answer: lovelace parameters above MAX_* are refused.
Overpaying compute on a wrong Koios answer: price_mem and price_step outside [0, MAX] are refused.
Overpaying reference-script fees: a reference-script price above 150 lovelace a byte, or a negative one, is refused.
Guessing a DRep deposit: a missing or out-of-range value reads as None, so a DRep registration refuses.
Reading anything other than constructor 0 with exactly two 48-byte fields (and nothing after) as a register.
A stranger's uncached token (decimals null) making a whole response unreadable, a stuck state.
A stranger's deeply nested datum or reference script hitting serde_json's 128-level limit and making a response unreadable.
A role, index or account of 2^31 or more silently selecting hardened derivation, which would give a different key and address.

checked_ok: Seedelf prover against the deployed verifier (5b82530 lib/schnorr.ak and validators/wallet.ak): same transcript order g, g_r, u, vkh, hashed with blake2b-224 over raw bytes. The prover hex-decodes the concatenation, and every part is checked to be whole bytes (48, 48, 48, 28).

Scalar encodings: c is the 28-byte hash read big-endian (left-padded to 32), so below 2^224, which is below q. z = r + c·sk is written as 32 canonical big-endian bytes. stdlib v2.2.0 scalar.new takes 0 ≤ n < q at any length, so every proof the prover makes decodes on chain.
Proof redeemer field order: core data_structures.rs:54-69 writes Constr 0 [z_b, g_r_b, vkh], matching the deployed `Proof` type.
vkh binding: create_proof refuses anything but 28 bytes; core `proven` passes the one-time signer's hash; the Lovejoin private withdraw (wasm lovejoin.rs:2893-2908) binds a fresh one-time key.

Hedged nonce (proof_nonce): HMAC-SHA-512 keyed by sk over fixed-length tag‖g‖u‖vkh‖32 random bytes, reduced from 512 bits (negligible bias), zero refused. Two different statements can never share a nonce, even if the random source fails.
Re-randomization: the same d goes on both points (register.rs:150-154). d is uniform (blstrs Scalar::random rejection-samples). The input points are subgroup-checked by from_compressed.

blstrs 0.7.1 G1Affine::from_compressed checks both on-curve and subgroup membership. blst refuses non-canonical encodings (x ≥ p, bad flag bits, infinity with other bits set), so is_owned's comparison of hex compressed points is sound.

is_owned: an identity generator or public value is owned by no key. A generator that doesn't decompress gives Err, and every caller treats that as not owned: Rust callers via unwrap_or(false), the extension's ownedUtxos and ownRegister by catching it. A stranger's junk datum never stops a scan.

Lovejoin Schnorr against 29573c5 hash.ak, schnorr.ak and bls.ak: blake2b-256 over DOMAIN‖0x01‖g‖u‖t‖ctx; c reduced mod r through two 128-bit halves (exact); z is 32 canonical bytes. The arguments are base=a and u=b, as mix_logic.ak:142 calls `schnorr.verify(mix_input.a, mix_input.b, proof, ctx)`.

Sigma-OR against sigma_or.ak and hash.ak: preimage DOMAIN‖0x03‖N(1 byte)‖a‖b‖(a'ᵢ,b'ᵢ)…‖(t0ᵢ,t1ᵢ)…‖ctx; raw 32-byte challenge shares XOR to the hash, satisfying xor32's length checks; per-branch c is taken mod r; simulated commitments are [z]a − [c]a'; N is in [2, 255].

RFC 6979 derive_nonce: bits2int shifts right by one bit for the 255-bit order; bits2octets reduces mod r; the K/V steps and the retry loop follow §3.2; the nonce is in [1, r). The message binds everything in the challenge except t, which r determines, so a deterministic nonce never meets two challenges.

Lovejoin proofs are pinned byte for byte by Lovejoin's known-answer vectors (30 provedlog cases, the sigma-OR cases, 84 negatives). There is no separate DH-tuple prover; dhtuple.ak is not called by any validator.
Seedelf and Lovejoin proofs can't be passed off as each other: different hashes, layouts and domain tags. Their nonces come from independent HMACs keyed by the same x.
cardano.rs: the Icarus master key (PBKDF2-HMAC-SHA512, password "", salt the entropy, 4096 rounds, 96 bytes, then normalize_bytes_force3rd) equals pallas-wallet 0.35.1 from_bip39_mnenomic.

cardano.rs paths: 1852'/1815'/account'/role/index; DRep key 3/0 per CIP-105; base address is payment role/index with stake 2/0; testnet flag maps to network 0. The one-time account 24301' is kept out of public accounts in the extension (preferences.ts isAccountIndex, accounts.ts:358).

derivation.rs (frozen): scalar_from_okm's Horner reduction over u64 limbs is exact. HKDF expand uses its own zeroizing HMAC. parse_phrase's 2×len capacity can't be outgrown, because Unicode lowercasing grows a word by at most 1.5× (İ: 2 bytes to 3).

register_of_datum reads token by token (no recursion). minicbor 0.25.1 checks every length (u64_to_usize, checked_add before get), so no datum can panic it. It accepts and refuses the same shapes as the extension's chain.ts registerOf.

Koios rows: a deep datum or reference-script JSON is taken raw. Unknown deep fields are skipped without the 128-level limit (pinned by koios.rs's unit test). decimals null reads 0. reference_script in an odd shape still counts as a script.
ProtocolParameters::from_koios: every bound uses checked or u128 arithmetic. Ratio::exact handles exponents, strings and floats and refuses negatives and overflow.

No reachable panic or trap in seedelf-crypto or seedelf-koios under wasm-release's overflow checks, except the unused `prove` (r1#3). eprintln! in extract_bytes_with_logging is a no-op on wasm32-unknown-unknown (Rust 1.98.1 std's unsupported stdio returns Ok).

The WebAssembly uses only seedelf-koios's types and parsers, never its HTTP functions (the TS fetches). The CLI's reqwest has a 10 s connect and 30 s total timeout. The giveme.my answer is parsed in core collateral_signature on bytes (no char-boundary slicing). An Ogmios 400 answer becomes an error in Budgets::from_ogmios, never empty budgets.
No secret in a Debug or error string in either crate. CardanoAccount has no Debug, icarus_master's error is pallas's key-shape enum, and register and proof errors carry only public bytes or lengths.

Randomness: getrandom's js backend (crypto.getRandomValues). Mix witnesses are drawn nonzero (core nonzero_scalar). Fisher-Yates is fed from OsRng with negligible modulo bias. One-time keys are HKDF(sk, fresh 32-byte seed).
notes:
Wiping (settled; new facts). architecture.md:79 already accepts one leak as best effort: the proof nonce's HMAC, keyed by the Seedelf scalar (schnorr.rs:66), leaves sk XOR the HMAC pads in freed heap. That is cryptoxide 0.5.1 hmac.rs:24-29 and 57-63: i_key and o_key are Vecs with no Drop. That list leaves out three more.
- lovejoin.rs's hmac_sha256 (a cryptoxide Hmac) is keyed by RFC 6979's K in derive_nonce (lovejoin.rs:142-155). K1 and K2 left in freed memory give V and the nonce r of an owner-withdraw proof, and with that proof's public z and c, the Seedelf key x = (z−r)/c.
- The same function is keyed by the mix witness (lovejoin.rs:290). The witness ties that box to its output.
- wasm/src/lib.rs:2057 one_time_key calls cryptoxide's hkdf_expand (hkdf.rs:53-76). Its HMAC holds the PRK, from which every one-time key follows given a seed, and its `t` Vec holds T(1), the one-time key's own 32 bytes. Both are freed unwiped, while architecture.md:73 lists 'the one-time keys' material' as wiped.

One zeroizing HMAC (derivation.rs:169-183, made generic over SHA-256 and SHA-512) would cover all four call sites. Memory imaging is out of SECURITY.md's scope, so this is not reported as a finding.

seedelf-crypto/README.md:7 links 'the on-chain verifier' to seedelf-contracts/lib/schnorr.ak on main, which is the never-deployed revision (stdlib v4, scalar.from_bytes). The deployed verifier is 5b82530's. The Fiat-Shamir is identical, so the prover matches both, but the link should name 5b82530 (D1).

For the T1 lens: Register::is_valid (register.rs:199-224) never returns Ok(false). blstrs from_compressed (g1.rs:337-340) already refuses off-curve and torsion points, so is_valid errors instead, and the explicit checks at register.rs:141-147 and 220-223 can never fail. Every caller treats Err as not valid (is_payable's unwrap_or(false), create_proof's ?, CLI mint's ?), so behavior is right. A mutant of those lines will survive because the real guard is from_compressed.

Asset.decimals is a u8 (koios.rs:128). A value over 255, or a negative one, fails the whole row set handed to the WebAssembly ('bad request'). Koios and the data layer take decimals from the CIP-26 registry (development.md:329), which keeps 0–255, so honest rows fit. If either source ever took CIP-68 decimals (any integer, chosen by the minter), one stranger's token at a Seedelf would stop every private build (E6 and the data layer's owner).

The CLI's credential_utxos reads every user's contract rows, so its offset loop also assumes Koios's page is exactly 1,000 rows. It sends no `limit` and stops only on an empty page. The extension sends limit=1000 and stops on a short page (koios.ts:1331-1339). This is part of r1#1's fix.

Not traced: the vectors' provenance (cardano_account.json from cardano-sdk, seedelf_key_v1.json, lovejoin_v1.json from Lovejoin's TS prover). The tests compare against them byte for byte, and I took that on trust.
